version.changelog:
**Major update: Booking flow now requires payment only at the appointment (no upfront payment), and support for card payments in advance has been removed.**

- Eliminated upfront/Stripe payment: customers now pay the cleaner directly (cash or card) at the appointment.
- Removed all references to "pay now" options, Stripe, and customer credentials from flow and documentation.
- Booking workflow and available tools simplified to reflect a pay-at-appointment only process.
- Adjusted safety rules and error handling for the new payment expectations.
- Only these API tools are now supported: `check_availability`, `initiate_booking`, and `check_booking_status`.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: claw-cleaning
Version: 1.0.5

The skill provides a legitimate interface for booking apartment cleaning services in San Francisco via an external MCP server (https://claw.cleaning/mcp). It includes clear safety instructions for the agent, such as requiring explicit user confirmation before booking and validating addresses. No malicious code, data exfiltration, or suspicious obfuscation was found.

llm.summary: The skill's requests and instructions are coherent with its stated purpose (booking weekend SF cleanings); it does not ask for credentials or install anything, but it will transmit customers' PII (name, email, address) to an external MCP endpoint that accepts unauthenticated calls.

dimensions.detail: Name, description, listed tools (check_availability, initiate_booking, check_booking_status), and the MCP endpoint all align with the stated purpose of booking SF weekend cleanings. No unrelated binaries, env vars, or installs are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions are narrowly scoped to the booking workflow (query availability, collect date/time/address/name/email, confirm, call initiate_booking). However, the skill requires sending personal data (full street address, name, email) to an external MCP server at https://claw.cleaning/mcp over an unauthenticated transport. The SKILL.md also instructs the user to add the endpoint as an MCP connector if not already present — that action delegates network access to the external service and should be done only if the endpoint/operator is trusted.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files; this is instruction-only and does not write files or fetch remote binaries. Lowest-risk install profile.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables, credentials, or config paths are requested. The data the skill sends (address, name, email) is necessary for bookings and is proportional to the function, but it is still PII that is transmitted off-device.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request elevated persistent privileges or modify other skills. Autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default) but not combined with any broad credential access.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says — book weekend apartment cleanings in San Francisco — and it does not request credentials or install code. Before installing or using it, be aware that the agent will transmit personal details (street address, name, email) to the external MCP endpoint https://claw.cleaning/mcp, which is described as accepting unauthenticated calls. Only use this skill if you trust the claw.cleaning operator; review any privacy policy or operator contact (connor@getcolby.com) if uncertain. If you’re uncomfortable sharing PII or allowing the agent to add a custom MCP connector, don’t enable the skill or ask the vendor for an authenticated/official integration first.
